offers.name: ASUS Vivobook Go 15 15.6" Laptop - Cool Silver (Intel Core i3-N305/8GB RAM/256GB UFS/Windows 11 Home)

praises: $499.95 for a 15.6" FHD clamshell with an SSD-class drive is the cheapest real laptop money can buy in Canada
i3-N305's 8 E-cores handle browsing, Office, and streaming smoothly and completely silently
Best battery of the Vivobook family for light use — Alder Lake-N draws almost nothing
1.63 kg with a numpad; fine as a kid's or grandparent's first Windows laptop
Full HDMI and USB-A ports — no dongle drawer needed for a classroom or guest machine
complaints: 256GB UFS storage is slow and small — Windows updates and a phone backup nearly fill it
Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) 1x1 only in 2026; oldest wireless in this family
8GB soldered DDR4: no upgrade path at all
English-only keyboard (no French legend) unlike the bilingual CA siblings
UHD 24EU graphics are hopeless for anything 3D or game-adjacent

standouts: Cheapest FHD Windows laptop in the dataset at $499.95 — the default answer for a sub-$500 gift
dealbreakers: UFS storage + Wi-Fi 5 + soldered 8GB: acceptable at $499.95, indefensible at any higher price
design_philosophy: A floor-price machine: ASUS takes the Go 15 chassis and drops in Alder Lake-N — eight little E-cores with a phone-grade UFS storage interface — to hit a psychological $499 price point. Every cost cut is deliberate (Wi-Fi 5, soldered 8GB, UFS, English keyboard) and every one is forgivable only because of that price. It is a browser/email/video terminal that happens to run Windows.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-vivobook.md). Platform-anchored on Alder Lake-N i3-N305 like the Aspire Lite 15 N350 anchor (15.json): productivity 3.6 (8 E-cores, weak single-thread), gaming 1.0 (24EU UHD). UFS storage + soldered 8GB + Wi-Fi 5 drive the low upgradability/port scores. Panel unstated, assumed ~220-nit TN class. Image URL best-guess BBY CDN pattern.
